pillars.name: The cost of asking
pillars.definition: What the current application system costs the organizations doing the work — hours, dollars, and access — and what a common application changes. Concrete and quantified: 40-hour applications, 19 pages for a $5,000 grant, a new portal per funder.
in_scope: what funders actually need to know to decide
access for organizations without a warm introduction
pillars.why_now: It is the argument Iara has the most first-party evidence for (26,000 nonprofits on one profile) and the one where the sector's own norms have already moved her way — a long application is now the outlier that has to explain itself.

pillars.name: Who actually holds the pen
pillars.definition: The structural difference between consulting a community and letting it decide — deciding bodies vs advisory bodies, proximity as due diligence, and what pooled and collaborative funds look like when the power is real.
pillars.why_now: Funders keep asking what participatory grantmaking looks like when it's real, and Iara has on-the-record interviews with the people running it — a supply of specifics almost nobody else can publish.

pillars.name: Money that isn't a grant
pillars.definition: The instruments between a grant and a market-rate investment — PRIs, catalytic capital, revolving loans, impact deposits — and the readiness gap that keeps mandated capital from landing anywhere.
pillars.why_now: Foundation investment committees are carving out catalytic slices and cannot find anywhere to deploy them, and Iara is going through the readiness process herself right now — a first-person view of the gap while it's live.

incumbent.how_we_differ: Iara argues the demand side has to be *built with grants* — a claim the supply-side incumbents don't make.

pillars.name: Transactional so you can be transformative
pillars.definition: The unglamorous machinery between a decision and a dollar — dockets, reviewer scores, compliance screening, banking details, disbursement lag — and what reclaiming that time makes possible.
in_scope: what staff time gets spent on
pillars.why_now: This is where the product lives, so it needs a disciplined share of the mix — enough to be credible on operations, not so much that the feed reads like a demo.

pillars.name: Who gets to build for this sector
pillars.definition: Why almost nobody builds serious technology for philanthropy, what it means that the sector's tools are assembled from other people's software, and the case for infrastructure built by people inside the problem.
in_scope: nonprofit tech and who funds it
pillars.why_now: It is the identity pillar — it explains why JustFund is a nonprofit and why Iara is credible on everything else. Small share, high leverage.

pillars.name: Building the thing while running it
pillars.definition: Leadership and team practice — failing forward, debriefs, perpetual pivot. Performs well and is authentically hers, but reaches peers rather than funders. Capped at roughly one post a month.
out_of_scope: anything that displaces a primary slot
